selection_policy.criterion: smallest implemented Table 4 row whose author-reported forgery classical bits meet the 128-bit classical baseline; PARAM-III is retained for a >=192-bit baseline

candidates.name: PARAM-I
candidates.rationale: smallest Table 4 row, but 100-bit target and 103/93-bit reported forgery are below the 128-bit classical baseline
caveats: q>2*gamma fails under the natural Q mapping

candidates.name: PARAM-II
candidates.rationale: smallest implemented Table 4 row with author-reported forgery above 128-bit classical (171/155) and key recovery 178/161; standard-deviation reading has a non-null first-issuance bridge
caveats: q>2*gamma fails under the natural Q mapping

candidates.name: PARAM-III
candidates.rationale: high-security option for a >=192-bit baseline: 242/219-bit reported forgery, 255/232-bit key recovery; heavier d=4 profile
caveats: q>2*gamma fails under the natural Q mapping

candidates.name: STATIC-N1024-D4
candidates.rationale: larger n could raise lattice security, but current FourierSchurPlan/Schur resource gates require n<=512 and no reproduced security estimate exists for this construction

candidates.name: STATIC-P-INCREASE
candidates.rationale: increasing p alone can make Q>2*gamma but the HNF head and signing Schur geometry scale with Q; fixed Table 4 signature widths no longer cover the user-key class, so this is not a valid correctness-preserving security profile
caveats: widths/gamma would need a new allocation

selected.name: PARAM-II
selected.rationale: smallest implemented Table 4 row with author-reported forgery above 128-bit classical (171/155) and key recovery 178/161; standard-deviation reading has a non-null first-issuance bridge
caveats: q>2*gamma fails under the natural Q mapping

known_gaps: author target/forgery bits are reports, not reproduced estimates
the paper's q>2*gamma condition is not met by Q under the natural mapping
Q/2Q, zeta factor1/factor2, r/sigma unit and Algorithm 4 d/f ambiguities remain
ring-HNF/CRT/subfield attack costs and NIST category are not established
scope: research security baseline selection; not a formal admission
